Voward adds a planning pause and clear time limits before selected apps and websites. It is a private self-management tool—not medical treatment or a diagnostic device. If digital use causes significant distress, sleep loss, unsafe behavior, or loss of control, consider seeking help from a qualified mental-health professional.

1. Review the disclosure, then grant only the permissions you accept.
2. Choose restricted apps from the installed-app picker and add domain/path rules for sites.
3. Set a daily budget in minutes and a default planned session.
4. Set a deactivation key. At each gate, write a purpose, choose a duration, wait, and confirm again.
5. Review whether sessions ended early or reached their limit; adjust gradually.

One budget second always buys one second of restricted use. The balance carries at most one daily allowance and can never fall below zero or borrow from a future day. When today’s allowance is depleted, no new restricted session can start. The re-entry pause grows logarithmically with sessions; it never changes a quoted session price. Domain rules match the domain and subdomains. A path matches only that path and its subtree; a configured query must match exactly. Use keyword:text only when broad text matching is intentional.

The recovery key is the only in-app way to deactivate active protection. There is no timer or charging bypass. For stronger commitment, have someone you trust create and keep the key. The optional uninstall guard adds friction but cannot turn a normal Android installation into an unbreakable kiosk. Accessibility can observe foreground app/window content and supported browser address text. Data stays on-device unless you explicitly export it.

1. Set a daily allowance, a default session length, and a real-life goal.
2. Choose at least one protected app or website.
3. Enable the required Attention Firewall accessibility service. Device Admin and notifications are optional.
4. Create a recovery key, review the setup summary, and activate protection.

At the gate, name a specific purpose and choose 1–60 minutes. Start the pause, then review the plan and explicitly choose Open intentionally or Not now. Finishing the timer never opens protected content automatically. Leaving the gate or choosing Not now returns you to Home.

One allowance second buys one second of approved protected use. A session ends at the smaller of its planned duration or the allowance remaining when it starts. Unused allowance carries forward only up to one daily allowance, and the balance never becomes negative. Repeat entries increase only the next pause; they do not change the cost of a quoted session.

Choose apps from the installed-app picker. For websites, example.com covers that domain and subdomains; example.com/news covers that path and its subtree; and a configured query must match exactly. Use keyword:shorts only for an intentionally broad match. A strict rule stays blocked regardless of remaining allowance. Deactivate protection before editing any rule.

The Attention Firewall accessibility service observes foreground apps, window content, and supported browser address text so it can enforce your rules. Device Admin uninstall friction and notifications are optional. Rules, settings, and usage counters stay on-device. Configuration export creates a JSON file you choose and excludes the recovery key, active-protection state, current allowance balance, usage counters, and temporary approvals. Purpose text entered at the gate is not stored.

The recovery key is the only in-app way to deactivate protection; it cannot be displayed or recovered, and there is no timed or charging bypass. For stronger commitment, let someone you trust create and keep it. Critical emergency and device-recovery apps cannot be selected for protection. Android accessibility is not kiosk mode, so optional uninstall protection adds friction rather than an absolute guarantee.
Strict rules ignore the remaining allowance. Access stays blocked until you deactivate protection.
